findings.reason: the section's central measurement can be unrunnable as written, and a node that finds too few single names must either ask the lead or silently substitute names, changing what the gate measures.
findings.text: bullet 1's gate rests on "at least 60 single-member names drawn at random across every domain file that holds one", but no cited artifact counts single-member names: §1's census reports species families of three or more members only (20 families, 281 names), §2's committed label set carries min_members 3 and 2,086 member ids over 197 families against 1,975 published names, and the operator census gives per-domain totals without family size. A node therefore cannot show the draw is possible — 60 single names spread over the files, and the count in each — before it is the thing being measured

findings.reason: the section passes or fails on an absolute bar whose two readings (all labelled names with a fallback versus decided names only) differ in both directions, so the node must choose the definition that decides its own verdict.
findings.text: bullet 3 requires "the accuracy under the widened options ... is at least the 0.597 floor that plan fixed", a floor measured on 150 labelled names with no confidence floor and no stored-domain fallback, while bullet 1 now fixes a different basis (a below-floor name counts at its stored domain) and bullet 4 applies that fallback to single names; bullet 3 states no basis, and the calibration names are Data Dictionary paths, for which a "stored domain" may not exist at all

response_events.note: §5 now cites the committed blind sheet: 70 single names drawn from the 1,370 published names that share their pattern with no other, labelled by two readers

done_when-1.note: §5 now cites the committed blind sheet: 70 single names drawn from the 1,370 published names that share their pattern with no other, labelled by two readers

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — sn-catalog-grouping resolves and carries the 0.560 (84 of 150) and 0.597 figures §5 quotes at its lines 415 and 424; the evidence directory resolves; the 698-of-1,975 and 28-domain-file counts reconcile against the operator census.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's primary gate draws "at least 60 single-member names ... across every domain file that holds one" while neither the plan nor the evidence it cites states how many single-member names exist or how they fall across the 28 domain files; and bullet 3's absolute 0.597 bar does not state the basis. Both are findings below.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the label set and gate log are committed under docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-per-family/, which exists and already holds §2's label set and decision logs; no temporary or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; every named string is a catalog name, a domain file or an evidence path.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (options bounded by a name's own Data Dictionary sources, so a source-bound answer cannot be escaped) matches §1's mechanism statement and its two named examples; the widened option set is decidable per family and the planted-name control in bullet 7 can fail. The two defects found are in how the gate is specified, not in the mechanism.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 delivers one thing: the option set grows beyond a name's source domains, decided by the one family decision §2 builds, with no second decision and no separate write path added.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — meta declares s5 depends on s2 and s3 depends on s2 and s5; the followup body states the same order (§5 waits for §2; §3 waits for §2 and §5), and every target resolves.
